description: Fully functional Bitcoin hardware wallet on ESP32-S3. Hardware: 128x64 SSD1306 OLED (I2C SDA=GPIO8, SCL=GPIO9), two buttons (BTN_CONFIRM=GPIO1, BTN_CANCEL=GPIO2), NXP SE051C2 secure element (replacing ATECC608B, same I2C bus), WiFi for OTA (dev only). Firmware is Arduino-framework C++ targeting ESP32-S3. All cryptographic key material must never leave the secure element.

userStories.title: NXP SE051C2 I2C HAL and Driver
userStories.description: As a firmware engineer, I need a hardware abstraction layer for the NXP SE051C2 secure element so all higher-level crypto and key operations have a stable interface to call.
acceptanceCriteria: SE051C2 initialises successfully over I2C (address 0x48) on Wire SDA=GPIO8 SCL=GPIO9

HAL exposes: se051_init(), se051_get_random(buf, len), se051_ecdsa_sign(keyId, hash, sig), se051_schnorr_sign(keyId, hash, sig), se051_store_key(keyId, keyMaterial), se051_delete_key(keyId), se051_get_pubkey(keyId, pubkey)
All HAL calls return typed error codes (SE_OK, SE_ERR_COMM, SE_ERR_AUTH, SE_ERR_LOCKED)
I2C error retry logic: 3 retries with 50 ms back-off before returning SE_ERR_COMM
A self-test routine (se051_selftest()) returns SE_OK on genuine NXP SE051C2
Unit: se051_get_random produces 32 bytes with no repeated all-zero or all-FF output across 10 calls
Compile with -DUSE_SE051 flag; stub HAL compiled under -DUSE_SE_STUB for CI builds
userStories.notes: SE051C2 uses GlobalPlatform SCP03 secure channel. Use NXP's SE05x Arduino library or port the SE05x_API from the NXP IoT-Agent SDK. ATECC608B stubs can remain for CI.

userStories.title: True-Random BIP39 Seed Generation via SE TRNG
userStories.description: As a user setting up a new wallet, I want the device to generate a cryptographically secure 24-word BIP39 mnemonic using entropy from the SE051C2 hardware TRNG so my seed is never predictable.
acceptanceCriteria: 256-bit entropy sourced exclusively from se051_get_random()
Entropy passed through BIP39 checksum (SHA-256 first 8 bits appended) to produce 264-bit word-index sequence
Word indices map to the BIP39 English wordlist (2048 words) stored in flash as a const char* array
Output is exactly 24 words separated by spaces, stored only in RAM (never written to flash or EEPROM)
Mnemonic buffer zeroed with memset_s() equivalent after use
Function signature: bool bip39_generate(char wordlist[24][9]) returns true on success
Compile-time assert: BIP39_WORDLIST_SIZE == 2048
userStories.notes: BIP39 wordlist can be embedded as a PROGMEM array on ESP32-S3. Use micro-ecc or mbedTLS SHA-256 already available in ESP-IDF.

userStories.title: Secure Key Storage: Seed → SE051C2 Key Objects
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the BIP39 master seed to be derived into a BIP32 root key and stored inside the SE051C2 as an EC key object so private key material never exists in ESP32-S3 RAM beyond the initial setup ceremony.
acceptanceCriteria: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 (BIP39) used to derive 64-byte master seed from mnemonic + optional passphrase
BIP32 master private key (k) and chain code (c) derived from master seed via HMAC-SHA512('Bitcoin seed' || seed)
Master private key stored in SE051C2 as key object ID = 0x01 using se051_store_key()
Chain code stored in SE051C2 key object ID = 0x02
After successful SE storage, seed bytes zeroed in RAM using volatile memset pattern
se051_get_pubkey(0x01) returns the correct compressed 33-byte secp256k1 master public key
A wallet_is_initialized() function returns true only if both objects 0x01 and 0x02 exist in SE
Storage failure causes immediate error screen and aborts setup; no partial state persists
userStories.notes: SE051C2 supports ECC key injection. Chain code may need to be stored as a binary file object (not a key object) since it is symmetric data.

userStories.title: BIP32/44/84/86 HD Key Derivation Engine
userStories.description: As a bitcoin-protocol engineer, I need an HD derivation engine that generates child public keys and derivation paths for Legacy, Native SegWit, and Taproot address types so the wallet can produce correct Bitcoin addresses without exposing private keys.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported derivation paths: m/44'/0'/0'/0/n (P2PKH), m/84'/0'/0'/0/n (P2WPKH), m/86'/0'/0'/0/n (P2TR)
Public-key-only child derivation (BIP32 public child key derivation) performed on ESP32-S3 using master public key + chain code from SE
Private child key derivation for signing is performed inside SE051C2 via hardened path unwrapping; private key never leaves SE
hd_derive_pubkey(path, index, pubkey_out) returns 33-byte compressed pubkey
Derives up to address index 999 without performance issue (< 200 ms per derivation)
Test vector: BIP32 test vector 1 (seed = 000102...) produces expected xpub at m/0'/1
Address index persisted in NVS (ESP32 Non-Volatile Storage); increments on each new address reveal
userStories.notes: Use the micro-ecc or trezor-crypto secp256k1 implementation. Hardened derivation requires the SE to compute the HMAC-SHA512 step internally.

userStories.title: PIN Setup and Entry UI (2-Button Interface)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to set a 6-digit PIN on first boot and enter it on every subsequent boot so that physical access to the device does not immediately grant access to my funds.
acceptanceCriteria: First-boot PIN setup: CONFIRM increments current digit (0-9 wrap), CANCEL confirms digit and advances to next position
PIN is 6 digits; progress shown as filled/empty circles on OLED (e.g. '●●●○○○')
PIN entry screen displayed on every boot before any wallet function is accessible
PIN hash (HMAC-SHA256 with device UID as key) stored in SE051C2 as a binary object (ID=0x03)
Correct PIN unlocks wallet state; incorrect PIN shows attempt counter (e.g. '2 of 5 attempts')
After 5 incorrect attempts, trigger wallet_factory_reset() and display 'WALLET WIPED'
PIN verification completes in < 500 ms
PIN change accessible from Settings menu after successful PIN authentication
userStories.notes: Store attempt counter in SE051C2 monotonic counter to prevent counter reset by reflashing NVS. CONFIRM/CANCEL button roles are swapped here vs. navigation: CONFIRM = increment digit, CANCEL = select digit.

userStories.title: Mnemonic Display Ceremony (Word-by-Word)
userStories.description: As a new user, I want the device to show me my 24-word seed phrase one word at a time on the OLED so I can write it down securely without the full phrase ever being visible at once.
acceptanceCriteria: Mnemonic display state shows: word number (e.g. 'Word 7 of 24'), word index in BIP39 list, and the word itself in large text (textSize 2)
CANCEL advances to next word; CONFIRM on word 24 exits to verification step
After display, verification step: device picks 3 random word positions and asks user to confirm each via CONFIRM/CANCEL scroll
Verification failure returns to word display from word 1
Verification success writes wallet_initialized flag to NVS and proceeds to PIN setup (US-005)
Display auto-dims (OLED off) after 30 s of no button press during ceremony; any button press restores
Mnemonic RAM buffer is zeroed immediately after verification passes
userStories.notes: Word verification picks random indices; use se051_get_random() for index selection. This prevents the user from skipping the backup step.

userStories.title: Wallet Restore from BIP39 Mnemonic
userStories.description: As a returning user whose device was reset, I want to restore my wallet by entering my 24-word BIP39 mnemonic on the device using the 2-button interface so I can regain access to my funds.
acceptanceCriteria: Restore flow accessible from boot menu when no wallet is initialised
Word entry: CANCEL scrolls through BIP39 wordlist alphabetically (A→Z→A), CONFIRM selects current word
Current partial word prefix shown on top line; matching words scroll below (up to 3 visible)
Entering a word not in BIP39 wordlist shows 'Invalid word' and rejects selection
After 24 words entered, BIP39 checksum validated; invalid checksum shows 'Bad checksum - retry'
Valid mnemonic proceeds to optional passphrase entry (US-013), then PIN setup (US-005)
Restore process arms a 5-minute timeout; if exceeded, display clears and returns to boot menu
Word entry state saves progress in RAM (not flash) so a button mis-press does not lose all progress
userStories.notes: Full BIP39 wordlist traversal with 2 buttons is slow. Consider letter-by-letter disambiguation: first button picks letter, second confirms, narrowing the word list progressively.

userStories.title: Bitcoin Address Generation (P2PKH, P2WPKH, P2TR)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the device to generate and display a Bitcoin receive address for the selected address type so I can receive funds to my hardware wallet.
acceptanceCriteria: address_generate(type, index, addr_out): generates address string for P2PKH (1...), P2WPKH (bc1q...), P2TR (bc1p...)
P2PKH: Hash160(pubkey) → Base58Check with version byte 0x00
P2WPKH: bech32_encode('bc', 0, Hash160(pubkey))
P2TR: bech32m_encode('bc', 1, x-only pubkey after BIP86 tweak)
Generated address displayed chunked across 2 lines of 21 chars on OLED
Address type selectable from Receive submenu using CANCEL to cycle types
Current address index shown (e.g. 'Address #3')
New address index stored in NVS after reveal; old addresses remain valid
Bech32/Bech32m checksum verified before display
userStories.notes: Use an existing bech32/bech32m encoder (e.g. from Bitcoin Core reference implementation, ported to C). BIP86 Taproot tweak: P = pubkey + H_tap(pubkey)*G where H_tap is tagged hash.

userStories.title: QR Code Rendering for Receive Address on SSD1306
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my receive address as a QR code on the OLED display so I can scan it with a phone camera without typing the address manually.
acceptanceCriteria: QR code generated for the current receive address string using QR code version auto-selection (alphanumeric mode for bech32)
QR rendered as a pixel-perfect bitmap on the 128x64 SSD1306; modules scaled to fit (max version 4 at 1px per module, centered)
CONFIRM shows QR; CANCEL returns to address text view
QR displayed with 2-module quiet zone
QR scannable by standard phone camera from at least 10 cm in normal indoor lighting (acceptance is manual visual test)
Library: use qrcode.h (ricmoo/QRCode) which is Arduino-compatible and PROGMEM-safe
If address is too long for a scannable QR at 128x64, display 'Address too long for QR - use text view' message
userStories.notes: SSD1306 128x64 can fit a QR version 3 (29x29 modules) at ~2px per module = 58px, leaving room for a border. Version 4 (33x33) at 1px is tight. Test with real camera.

userStories.title: PSBT v0/v2 Parser (BIP174/BIP370)
userStories.description: As a bitcoin-protocol engineer, I need a PSBT parser that can decode a partially-signed Bitcoin transaction from raw bytes so the device can display transaction details and sign inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: psbt_parse(buf, len, psbt_out) decodes a BIP174 PSBT v0 or BIP370 PSBT v2 from binary buffer

Parser extracts: version, global unsigned tx, per-input fields (previous txid, vout, sequence, BIP32 derivation, witness UTXO, sighash type), per-output fields (amount, scriptPubKey, BIP32 derivation)
Parser validates magic bytes (0x70736274ff for v0, 0x70736274fe for v2)
Malformed PSBT returns PSBT_ERR_INVALID with specific error code
psbt_get_total_input_value() and psbt_get_total_output_value() computed correctly from witness UTXOs
psbt_get_fee() = total_input - total_output; negative fee returns PSBT_ERR_INVALID
Parser handles PSBTs up to 4 KB (typical single-input transaction)
Test: parse the BIP174 example PSBT from the BIP specification and verify all fields
userStories.notes: Allocate PSBT struct on heap; free after signing. ESP32-S3 has 512 KB SRAM so 4 KB PSBTs are fine. No dynamic allocation during parsing; use fixed-size struct fields.

userStories.title: Transaction Review UI (Outputs, Fee, Destination)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see a clear summary of a transaction I am about to sign — including destination address, amount, and fee — on the OLED before I confirm, so I can verify the transaction details match my intent.
acceptanceCriteria: Transaction review screen shows: 'SEND', output amount in BTC (8 decimal places), fee in sats and sat/vB, destination address (chunked, scrollable with CANCEL)
If PSBT has multiple outputs, display each output sequentially; CANCEL scrolls through outputs
Fee shown in two formats: absolute sats and effective fee rate (sat/vB = fee_sats / vsize_vbytes)
vsize calculated as: (base_size + witness_size/4) rounded up
High-fee warning shown if fee_rate > 500 sat/vB: 'HIGH FEE - Confirm?' with inverted background
Change output identified by matching BIP32 derivation paths; labeled 'CHANGE' not shown as destination
CONFIRM on final output screen advances to signing prompt; CANCEL at any point returns to main menu
Display updates within 100 ms of receiving PSBT
userStories.notes: Multi-output PSBTs require a scrollable list pattern: maintain output_index in state, CANCEL increments, CONFIRM signs. Change detection requires wallet to know its own derivation paths.

userStories.title: PSBT Signing via SE051C2 (ECDSA + Schnorr)
userStories.description: As a user who has reviewed and confirmed a transaction, I want the device to sign it using the private key stored in the SE051C2 so the signature is produced without my private key ever appearing in ESP32-S3 RAM.
acceptanceCriteria: For each PSBT input: derive the correct child private key index from BIP32 path in the PSBT input map using se051 internal derivation
P2WPKH inputs: compute sighash per BIP143 (SHA256d of serialized segwit signing data); sign with ECDSA via se051_ecdsa_sign()
P2TR key-path inputs: compute sighash per BIP341 (tagged SHA256 of sigMsg); sign with Schnorr via se051_schnorr_sign()
DER-encode ECDSA signatures; Schnorr signatures are raw 64-byte format
Sighash type appended to each signature (SIGHASH_ALL = 0x01)
Signed PSBT has partial_sig or tap_key_sig field populated for each input
Signing sequence shows animated progress on OLED: 'Hashing...', 'Signing input 1/N...', 'Done'
If SE signing fails, show error code on display and do NOT return a partial PSBT
Signing completes in < 3 s per input
userStories.notes: BIP341 sighash requires SHA256 with tag 'TapSighash'. Pre-compute tagged hash prefix. Schnorr signing in SE051C2 requires the key to be an ECC P-256 key or custom BIP340 implementation — verify SE051C2 supports secp256k1 or add software Schnorr on top of SE ECDSA.

userStories.title: BIP39 Passphrase (25th Word) Support
userStories.description: As a privacy-conscious user, I want to optionally enter a BIP39 passphrase (25th word) during wallet setup or restore so I can have hidden wallets that cannot be discovered even if my mnemonic is found.
acceptanceCriteria: After mnemonic entry, display 'Add Passphrase? [YES/NO]'; CONFIRM = YES, CANCEL = NO
If YES: character-by-character entry using 2-button interface (CANCEL cycles character set A-Z/a-z/0-9/symbols, CONFIRM selects char, long-press CONFIRM = done)
Passphrase length 0–64 characters; display shows character count and last 3 entered chars + '***' masking
Passphrase combined with mnemonic in PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 as per BIP39 ('mnemonic' + passphrase)
Passphrase NOT stored anywhere (not in SE, not in NVS); must be re-entered each boot (by design)
If passphrase was set: boot flow prompts 'Enter Passphrase' after PIN unlock before wallet is usable
Empty passphrase (NO selection) = standard BIP39 derivation with '' passphrase
Passphrase RAM buffer zeroed immediately after seed derivation
userStories.notes: The passphrase is intentionally not stored. This is the standard BIP39 design. The user must remember it independently of the mnemonic.

userStories.title: USB CDC Serial Transport for PSBT Exchange
userStories.description: As a developer/user, I want to send a PSBT to the device over USB serial and receive the signed PSBT back so the device can be used as a signing device with a companion software wallet on a desktop computer.
acceptanceCriteria: ESP32-S3 USB CDC enabled (USB_CDC_ENABLED=1 in build config); appears as /dev/ttyACM0 or /dev/cu.usbmodem on host
Protocol: newline-delimited base64; device reads until '\n', decodes base64 to binary PSBT
After signing, device writes base64-encoded signed PSBT followed by '\n' back to host

Protocol framing: device sends 'READY
' after boot; host sends 'PSBT:<base64>
'; device replies 'SIGNED:<base64>
' or 'ERROR:<code>
'
If user rejects transaction on device, device sends 'REJECTED\n' to host
USB receive buffer 8 KB (handles typical PSBTs); overflow returns 'ERROR:OVERFLOW\n'
Serial transport does not interfere with ArduinoOTA (OTA only active when wallet not in signing mode)
Baud rate irrelevant for CDC (USB full-speed); document that any baud rate setting on host side is ignored
userStories.notes: ESP32-S3 has native USB, so use USB CDC directly (not UART-to-USB chip). Configure via ESP-IDF sdkconfig: CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_USB_CDC=y. Arduino: use USBSerial instead of Serial for CDC.

userStories.title: Address Verification Flow (Anti-Substitution)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the device to show me a receive address and require me to confirm it matches what is displayed on the companion app so I can detect address-substitution attacks by malware on the host computer.
acceptanceCriteria: Receive menu has 'Verify Address' option distinct from 'Show Address'
Verify flow: companion app sends address verification request over USB ('VERIFY:<address>\n')
Device derives the address at the same index and type, compares byte-for-byte with received address
If match: display full address on OLED with '✓ VERIFIED' indicator; user confirms with CONFIRM
If mismatch: display 'ADDRESS MISMATCH!' in large inverted text with an alarm pattern (rapid display flash 3x)
Device replies 'VERIFIED\n' or 'MISMATCH\n' to host after user response
Without companion app: standalone verify shows address in full; user must manually compare with their own records
Address type and index shown alongside address during verification
userStories.notes: This is a critical security feature. The whole point of a hardware wallet is that the address displayed on device is trusted. Always derive independently rather than displaying the host-provided address directly.

userStories.title: Anti-Phishing Device Pairing Code
userStories.description: As a user, I want the device to display a unique device pairing word (anti-phishing code) at boot that I can verify matches my registered code in the companion app so I can detect fake firmware or cloned devices.
acceptanceCriteria: On first setup, device generates a 4-word anti-phishing code using se051_get_random() mapped to BIP39 wordlist
Anti-phishing code stored in SE051C2 as binary object ID=0x04
At every boot, after PIN entry, device displays 'Device ID: [word1] [word2] [word3] [word4]' for 3 seconds
User must visually confirm this matches their registered code; no automatic check (human confirmation)
Anti-phishing code can be reset only via full factory reset (not from settings menu)
Anti-phishing code exported to companion app via USB on first setup ('PAIRING:<4words>\n')
Companion app should store and verify the code each connection; document this in comments
userStories.notes: This is a UX-layer protection. It cannot prevent a sophisticated attacker who modifies the firmware to display a fake code, but it raises the bar considerably. Document the threat model clearly.

userStories.title: PIN Lockout, Wipe, and Monotonic Attempt Counter
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the PIN attempt counter to be stored in the SE051C2 as a monotonic counter that cannot be reset by reflashing NVS or the ESP32-S3 firmware, so that brute-force PIN attacks are bounded by hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: PIN attempt counter stored in SE051C2 monotonic counter object (ID=0x05); increments before each PIN verification attempt
Counter reset to 0 only after successful PIN entry (requires unlocking SE with current PIN-derived credential)
After 5 failed attempts: se051_delete_key() called for all key objects (0x01–0x05), NVS erased, device reboots to factory state
Wipe sequence cannot be interrupted (watchdog-armed during wipe; if interrupted, wipe continues on next boot)
Display shows 'WALLET WIPED - Restore from seed' after wipe completes
Attempt count displayed as warning from attempt 3: 'Warning: N attempts remaining'
Wipe is irreversible from software; only mnemonic restore can recover funds
userStories.notes: The monotonic counter is the key security property here. Without it, an attacker can simply reflash NVS to reset the counter. SE051C2 supports monotonic counters natively.

userStories.title: Multi-Account HD Wallet (BIP44 Account Index)
userStories.description: As a power user, I want to manage multiple independent HD accounts (different BIP44 account indices) on the same seed so I can separate funds for different purposes without using multiple seeds.
acceptanceCriteria: Account selector accessible from main menu; displays 'Account 0', 'Account 1' ... 'Account 9'
CANCEL cycles through accounts 0–9; CONFIRM selects and switches active account
Active account index stored in NVS; restored on boot
All address generation and PSBT signing uses the active account's derivation path (m/84'/0'/ACCOUNT'/0/n)
Each account maintains independent address index in NVS (keyed by account number)
Account name customisation: 6-character label editable via 2-button input, stored in NVS
Maximum 10 accounts (indices 0–9); attempting to add 11th shows 'Max accounts reached'
Active account indicator shown on main menu header (e.g. 'COINCUBE [Acct 2]')
userStories.notes: BIP44 account hardened derivation: m/purpose'/coin_type'/account'/change/index. All accounts share the same master key in SE051C2; derivation happens per-request.

userStories.title: UTXO Coin Control (Input Selection for Signing)
userStories.description: As a privacy-conscious user, I want to select which UTXOs (unspent outputs) to include in a transaction I am signing so I can avoid merging coins from different sources and maintain transaction privacy.
acceptanceCriteria: Coin control menu shows list of UTXOs from the PSBT's inputs (txid truncated to 8 chars, vout, amount in sats)
CANCEL scrolls through UTXOs; CONFIRM toggles selection (selected = '✓', unselected = '○')
Only selected UTXOs are included in signing; unselected inputs are left unsigned in the returned PSBT
Total selected amount and estimated fee shown at bottom of coin control screen
If no UTXOs selected and user tries to confirm, show 'Select at least 1 input'
Coin control screen accessible before transaction review in the signing flow
PSBT inputs that are not owned by this wallet (no matching BIP32 derivation) shown as 'EXTERNAL - skip' and not selectable
Default: all owned inputs pre-selected
userStories.notes: Coin control is only meaningful when the PSBT has multiple inputs. If PSBT has 1 input, skip coin control screen and go directly to review.

userStories.title: Settings Menu (Display Timeout, Auto-Lock, Brightness)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a settings menu accessible from the main menu where I can configure display auto-off timeout, wallet auto-lock timeout, and OLED contrast so I can balance usability and security.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings menu items: Display Timeout, Auto-Lock Timeout, Display Contrast, Change PIN, About
Display Timeout: options 30s / 1m / 2m / 5m / Never; OLED off after timeout, any button wakes
Auto-Lock Timeout: options 1m / 5m / 15m / 30m / Never; locks wallet (requires PIN re-entry) after inactivity
Display Contrast: 0–255 in steps of 32 using SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC contrast command; previewed live
All settings persisted in NVS namespace 'settings'
Settings accessible only after PIN authentication
Change PIN flow: confirm current PIN, enter new PIN twice, compare; if mismatch show 'PINs do not match'
About screen shows: firmware version, build date, SE051C2 serial number (from se051_selftest()), BTC address type, active account
userStories.notes: Use esp_timer or FreeRTOS timers for auto-lock/display timeout. Activity resets both timers. Long-press CANCEL from main menu can be a shortcut to manual lock.

userStories.title: Factory Reset (Full Key and Settings Wipe)
userStories.description: As a user selling or repurposing my device, I want a factory reset option that irreversibly deletes all keys, PIN, settings, and pairing data so the next owner cannot access my funds.
acceptanceCriteria: Factory reset accessible from Settings menu (requires PIN authentication)
Double-confirmation required: 'Reset wallet? [CANCEL=No] [CONFIRM=Yes]' then 'Are you sure? This cannot be undone. [CANCEL=No] [CONFIRM=WIPE]'
Reset sequence: se051_delete_key() for IDs 0x01–0x05, NVS erase all namespaces, reboot
Wipe is watchdog-armed: if power is cut during wipe, device boots and detects partial wipe (wallet_is_initialized() returns false with missing SE objects), completes wipe on next boot
After reboot, device shows setup wizard as if new
Factory reset does NOT wipe firmware; only data
Reset operation takes < 5 s; progress shown as 'Wiping...' on OLED
userStories.notes: The double-confirmation is intentional friction to prevent accidental wipe. Consider requiring the user to hold CONFIRM for 3 seconds on the second confirmation.

userStories.title: Disable WiFi OTA in Production Builds
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need WiFi and OTA update capability to be disabled in production firmware builds so the hardware wallet has no wireless attack surface when deployed to end users.
acceptanceCriteria: Build flag -DPRODUCTION_BUILD disables all WiFi code paths (WiFi.begin, ArduinoOTA) via #ifdef guards
In production build, WiFi radio powered off at boot using esp_wifi_stop() and esp_wifi_deinit()
OTA update in production requires physical USB connection only (USB DFU or UART bootloader)
Development build (-DDEV_BUILD) retains WiFi OTA with password from secrets.h
Production build has no secrets.h dependency; secrets.h guarded by #ifdef DEV_BUILD
CI build matrix: compile both DEV_BUILD and PRODUCTION_BUILD to verify both compile without error
Production binary size should be smaller than dev binary (WiFi stack excluded): assert in CI that PRODUCTION_BUILD binary < 1.2 MB
README documents how to flash production vs dev firmware
userStories.notes: This is critical. A hardware wallet with WiFi is not a hardware wallet — it's a hot wallet in a box. The WiFi OTA is useful for development iteration but must be completely absent in production.

userStories.title: Firmware Secure Boot and Version Attestation
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need ESP32-S3 secure boot v2 enabled so the device only boots signed firmware, and a firmware version screen so users can verify they are running authentic software.
acceptanceCriteria: ESP32-S3 secure boot v2 enabled via sdkconfig: CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT=y, CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2_ENABLED=y
Signing key generated offline; public key hash burned into ESP32-S3 eFuses during manufacturing
Unsigned firmware rejected at boot (ESP32-S3 ROM verifier)
Flash encryption enabled: CONFIG_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED=y; NVS and firmware encrypted at rest
Firmware version embedded as const char* FIRMWARE_VERSION = "1.0.0" and shown in About screen
Build hash (first 8 bytes of SHA256 of firmware binary) displayed in About screen
SE051C2 reports its own serial/attestation certificate via se051_selftest(); serial shown in About screen
Document eFuse burning procedure in README for manufacturing; include key ceremony steps
userStories.notes: Secure boot eFuse burning is irreversible. Test the full flow in a dev environment before burning production keys. Once eFuses are burned, unsigned firmware will permanently brick the device.

userStories.title: Watchdog Timer and Safe Panic Recovery
userStories.description: As a firmware engineer, I need a hardware watchdog so that if the firmware hangs or crashes during a sensitive operation (e.g., signing), the device reboots to a safe state rather than remaining in an undefined state.
acceptanceCriteria: ESP32-S3 hardware watchdog (TWDT) enabled with 10-second timeout
Watchdog fed (esp_task_wdt_reset()) only in the main loop; any blocking operation > 10 s triggers reboot
On reboot after watchdog reset: display 'Device recovered - re-enter PIN' and clear any signing-in-progress state from NVS
Signing state machine uses NVS flag 'signing_active' set before signing, cleared after; if set on boot, assume crash and clear without committing PSBT
Panic handler (esp_set_panic_handler) logs panic reason to NVS (last 128 bytes) before reboot
Panic log accessible from About screen as 'Last crash: <reason>'
Stack overflow detection enabled: CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_CONFIG_STACK_DEPTH monitored
All ISRs and timer callbacks are minimal; no crypto operations in interrupt context
userStories.notes: The 'signing_active' NVS flag is the key recovery mechanism. It prevents returning a partially-signed PSBT if the device crashed mid-signature, which could confuse the host wallet.

userStories.title: RBF Flag Detection and Fee Bump Warning
userStories.description: As a user reviewing a transaction, I want the device to warn me if the transaction has the RBF (Replace-By-Fee) flag set so I am aware the recipient can see an unconfirmed payment that may be replaced.
acceptanceCriteria: PSBT parser detects RBF: any input with nSequence < 0xFFFFFFFE is flagged as RBF-enabled
Transaction review screen shows 'RBF: ON' or 'RBF: OFF' on the fee line
If RBF is ON: additional screen shown before signing prompt: 'RBF ENABLED - Tx can be replaced. Continue?' CONFIRM=Yes CANCEL=No
Locktime field parsed and displayed if non-zero: 'Locktime: YYYY-MM-DD' (if < 500000000) or 'Locktime: Block NNNN'
Segwit version shown per input: 'SegWit v0' (P2WPKH/P2WSH) or 'Taproot v1' (P2TR)
These metadata fields visible on the transaction details scroll view (CANCEL to scroll)
userStories.notes: RBF signalling is nSequence < 0xFFFFFFFE per BIP125. This is an informational feature; the device should sign RBF transactions normally after user acknowledgement.

userStories.title: Multi-Sig PSBT Co-Signing Support
userStories.description: As a user participating in a 2-of-3 multisig setup, I want the device to sign its input in a multi-sig PSBT and return the partially-signed result so the PSBT can be passed to other co-signers.
acceptanceCriteria: PSBT parser identifies multisig inputs via redeemScript or witnessScript analysis
For P2WSH multisig: device signs its input if a BIP32 derivation path in the input matches a key owned by this device
Device adds its partial_sig to the PSBT without finalising (finalisation requires M-of-N signatures)
Transaction review screen shows 'MULTISIG N-of-M' header when multisig input detected
Review shows: required signers (M), total signers (N), existing signatures count already in PSBT
Device does NOT attempt to finalize the PSBT if M sigs not yet reached; returns partially-signed PSBT
If device's key is not a participant in any input, show 'No inputs to sign - not a participant' and reject
Miniscript policy parsing not required; only standard M-of-N P2WSH and P2MS scripts
userStories.notes: Multi-sig is a stretch goal but important for advanced users. The key challenge is identifying which input key belongs to this device by matching BIP32 derivation paths in the PSBT.

userStories.title: Post-Quantum Status Screen (ML-KEM-512 Roadmap)
userStories.description: As a user concerned about quantum computing threats to Bitcoin, I want to see the device's post-quantum security status and roadmap so I understand the long-term security posture of the wallet.
acceptanceCriteria: PQC Status screen accessible from main menu (replaces the existing PQC_STATUS state)
Screen shows: current SE type ('NXP SE051C2'), current signature scheme ('secp256k1 ECDSA / Schnorr'), PQC readiness ('PQC: Roadmap - Phase 1')
Phase indicator: Phase 1 = Classical crypto (current), Phase 2 = Hybrid ECDSA+ML-KEM-512 (planned), Phase 3 = Full ML-KEM-512 (future)
NIST PQC standard shown: 'FIPS 203 ML-KEM-512' with status 'Not yet implemented'
Estimated quantum threat timeline note: 'BTC quantum risk: ~2030+ per NIST'
Screen scrollable (CANCEL advances lines) if content exceeds 64px height
Information is static/display-only; no interactive elements beyond BACK
userStories.notes: This screen is informational. Real PQC signing is a future firmware upgrade requiring SE051C2 firmware update or a new SE. The screen sets correct user expectations.

userStories.title: Wallet Balance Display (Live via Companion App)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the balance screen to show a live balance fetched from the companion app over USB rather than a hardcoded mock value, so I can see my actual on-chain balance.
acceptanceCriteria: On entering SHOW_BALANCE state, device sends 'BALANCE_REQUEST:<address>\n' over USB CDC for each address index 0..N
Companion app responds 'BALANCE:<confirmed_sats>:<unconfirmed_sats>\n'
Device aggregates responses and displays total confirmed balance in BTC and sats
Unconfirmed balance shown separately if non-zero: '+ N sats unconfirmed'
If USB not connected or no response within 2 s: display cached balance from NVS with '(cached)' label
Cache updated on each successful balance fetch; stored in NVS namespace 'balance'
Balance display shows last-updated timestamp if cached: 'Last sync: 2024-01-15'
Hardcoded mock balance removed from production builds; only present under -DMOCK_DATA flag
userStories.notes: The device itself has no network access in production mode. Balance is always fetched from the companion app or cached. The companion app is responsible for querying an Electrum server or block explorer API.

userStories.title: Scrollable Transaction History Display
userStories.description: As a user, I want to view a list of recent transactions on the device so I can quickly verify recent activity without opening the companion app.
acceptanceCriteria: TX History menu item added to main menu
Device requests 'TX_HISTORY:<address>\n' over USB; companion responds with up to 10 entries: 'TX:<txid_short>:<direction>:<amount_sats>:<confirmations>\n' per entry
Direction: '+' for received, '-' for sent
Each entry displayed as one OLED screen: 'RECEIVED' or 'SENT' header, amount in BTC, txid (first 8 + last 4 chars), confirmations
CANCEL scrolls to next transaction; CONFIRM returns to main menu
If no USB connection: show cached history from NVS (last 10 transactions, LRU eviction)
Confirmations shown as number if < 100; '100+' if >= 100; 'UNCONFIRMED' if 0
Zero-confirmation incoming transactions shown with 'UNCONFIRMED' warning label
userStories.notes: Transaction history storage in NVS: 10 * ~100 bytes = 1 KB, well within NVS limits. txid stored as 32 bytes; display only truncated version.

userStories.title: Firmware Integrity Self-Test on Boot
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I need the device to verify its own firmware integrity on every boot using a SHA-256 hash comparison so that any flash tampering is detected before the wallet is unlocked.
acceptanceCriteria: On boot (before PIN prompt), compute SHA-256 over the firmware partition (esp_partition_read loop)
Expected hash stored in SE051C2 as binary object ID=0x06 (written during factory provisioning)
If computed hash matches SE-stored hash: proceed to PIN entry; display 'Integrity OK ✓' for 1 s
If mismatch: display 'FIRMWARE TAMPERED!' with full OLED invert, sound buzzer if connected, refuse to proceed to PIN entry
Tamper state exits only via physical reset; device loops on tamper screen indefinitely
Self-test completes in < 3 s for 1 MB firmware partition
Factory provisioning script (Python) computes hash and writes to SE051C2 at end of manufacturing flashing step
Self-test can be skipped during development under -DSKIP_INTEGRITY_CHECK build flag
userStories.notes: This complements secure boot (US-023). Secure boot prevents unsigned firmware from booting; integrity check detects if signed but modified firmware is running (e.g., signed with a stolen key). Defense in depth.
